title: Marine Mammals of the California Current
description: Marine mammals of the California Current: their biodiversity and connections to California's physical, biological, and social systems.

title: Euler's Gem - An Introduction to Topology and its Applications
description: The goal of the seminar is to introduce you to the work of famous mathematicians, such as Pythagoras, Euclid, Euler, Gauss, Riemann, Noether, and Poincaré, through the book “Euler’s Gem: The Polyhedron Formula and the Birth of Topology”.

title: Hidden Figures of Mathematics
description: Explores contributions of women, first-generation scholars, and mathematicians from underrepresented groups whose work influenced modern mathematics. Through short readings, discussion, and accessible mathematical examples, the seminar highlights the role of diverse perspectives in scientific advancement. Emphasizes empowerment, community, and the value of discovering role models in STEM.

title: Beyond Picasso and Dalí: Spanish Women Artists
description: Spanish women artists, despite their significant contributions, have been overshadowed by contemporary figures such as Picasso and Dalí. Our Discovery Seminar offers a unique exploration of a lesser-known aspect of Spanish art and culture. Within their historical, political, and artistic contexts, students will explore the imaginative work of well-recognized personalities such as Maruja Mallo (1902-1995), Roser Bru (1923-2021), Lucinda Urrusti (1929-2023), Marta Palau (1934-2022), and Mar Caldas (1964).

title: If Books Could Kill: Spotting How and Why Some Books Mislead You
description: Using the popular podcast If Books Could Kill as a jumping off point, this seminar looks at how to spot misinformation, bias, misleading graphics and data, and evaluate claims made in best-selling books. Students will listen to specific podcast episodes and complete supplementary readings designed to help them go deeper.

title: Latin American Music in Motion
description: This seminar explores how music from Latin America travels, transforms, and shapes cultural experiences across the globe. Rather than focusing on specific styles, students will explore how music is created, shared, and enjoyed in different cultural contexts. Through listening exercises, discussion, and multimedia materials, the course introduces how sounds change as they move between places and audiences. No prior musical background is required.
